model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the coverage achieved by four different models—Llama-3B, Llama-3B + FT, Llama-1B, and Llama-1B + FT—as a function of the number of completions, denoted as $k$. The x-axis, labeled “Number of completions ($k$)”, is plotted on a logarithmic scale, spanning from $2^{20}$ to $2^{25}$, with tick marks at intervals of $2^1$ (i.e., powers of two). The y-axis, labeled “Coverage”, ranges from 0.4 to 0.8 in linear units. The blue solid line with circular markers represents Llama-3B, starting at approximately 0.42 coverage at $k = 2^{20}$ and increasing to nearly 0.85 at $k = 2^{25}$. The green dashed line with triangular markers represents Llama-3B + FT, beginning at approximately 0.43 coverage at $k = 2^{20}$ and rising to approximately 0.85 at $k = 2^{25}$. The light blue dashed line with diamond markers represents Llama-1B, starting at approximately 0.33 coverage at $k = 2^{20}$ and increasing to about 0.81 at $k = 2^{25}$. The light green dashed line with inverted triangular markers represents Llama-1B + FT, beginning at approximately 0.33 coverage at $k = 2^{20}$ and rising to approximately 0.81 at $k = 2^{25}$. All four lines show a general upward trend in coverage as $k$ increases, with Llama-3B and Llama-3B + FT achieving higher coverage than Llama-1B and Llama-1B + FT at equivalent values of $k$.
